text:
elena_cs: FYI onboarding check-in for Clipper — they see sporadic 429s during initial SDK preflight when a bunch of users hit the page at once. Happening in prod env, not repro locally.

jordan_eng: Thanks, can you paste a short sample of the logs (request id + upstream status) and the SDK build/version?

elena_cs: SDK: web-sdk@1.2.4, integration using ephemeral tokens via our ephemeral-token-proxy. Sample log: ```[2023-10-12T14:02:23Z] req=rx-7f3 upstream=preflight-edge status=429 reason=rate_limit window=1m```. Seen 10-20 hits/sec spikes.

jordan_eng: Hmm. Are these 429s all from same IP range or many client IPs? Also, are preflight requests identical (same route/headers) or vary by session?

elena_cs: Looks like many different client IPs (mobile + desktop). Preflight payloads are identical — just a quick capability check. They do a token refresh immediately after preflight.

nora_se: Two quick hypotheses: 1) our edge preflight endpoint is un-cached and fanouts to downstream auth which has a per-key burst window, 2) ephemeral-token refreshs are racing causing short lived token storms. Suggest: add short client-side caching for preflight (500ms-2s) + jitter token refresh backoff.

jordan_eng: Agree. Can you have the customer try client-side caching first? e.g. in web SDK set preflightCacheTTL=1500 and add jitter: 
```js
const backoff = 500 + Math.random() * 1000; // ms
setTimeout(refreshToken, backoff);
```
Also I'll enable temporary higher soft-limit on preflight route for their account while we validate.

elena_cs: Will ask Clipper to roll a canary with those SDK tweaks. I'll also give them a patch with preflightCacheTTL.

ops-bot: NOTE: Rate limit soft-lift applied to account clipper-inc for route /v1/preflight until 2023-10-12T15:00:00Z by jordan_eng

nora_se: If they still see spikes after client-side change, we should patch the proxy to add per-session token affinity and a small autoscale buffer on preflight workers. I can open a short-lived PR to add a configurable session affinity flag.

elena_cs: Clipper rolled the client change to 10% of traffic just now, initial results look promising (no 429s in the canary 30m window). Can we keep the soft-lift for another hour while they ramp? :thumbsup:

jordan_eng: Keeping soft-lift for +1h. If canary stays green, we'll drop it and push a note to the onboarding guide to recommend preflight caching + refresh jitter.

elena_cs: Awesome — I'll follow up with a short how-to for their engineers and add a snippet to the live onboarding checklist. Thanks everyone.
